topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture on cancer causation and states what students should learn.

topics.label: Mutations, clonal evolution and cancer susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arise and enable susceptible cells to evolve into cancers within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine evidence that environmental exposures influence cancer risk rather than cancer being solely a matter of inherited susceptibility or bad luck.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma illustrating the interaction between pathogens and cellular mutations.

topics.label: Mechanisms of environmentally induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental exposures produce DNA damage and mutations through mechanisms shaped by cellular metabolism and repair.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutation-bearing cells may require a growth-promoting environment before they develop into tumours.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how carcinogenic effects depend on the exposed tissue's biological context and consolidate this principle within the preceding account of carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Evidence linking exposures to human cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how observations and biological measurements from human populations can connect carcinogen exposure with cancer development.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess how experimental test systems detect carcinogenic potential and why their results may not capture cancer development in humans.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture's conclusions about environmental cancer risks and carcinogen assessment through the framing of everyday risk–benefit decisions.
